To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

THz light can be used to control both out-of-plane and high-frequency in-plane plasma waves in layered superconductors via two-plasmon excitations, which is a non-linear process that is strongly enhanced by the anisotropic nature of the Josephson coupling.

(i) THz light pulses can be used to excite both the low- and high-frequency Josephson plasma modes in cuprate superconductors, (ii) the non-linear response of the high-frequency Josephson plasmons is strongly affected by thermal fluctuations, (iii) the thermal effects are strongly anisotropic and are linked to the anisotropy and temperature dependence of the Josephson coupling constants.
the high-energy in- plane plasma waves of layered cuprates can be non-linearly excited with THz light pulses.

THz light is an ideal tool to study phase excitations in cuprate superconductors.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
THz light can selectively excite the phase mode in superconducting materials, and that this mode is the one that controls the superfluid properties.
the Josephson coupling is a crucial parameter to understand the non-linear response of layered superconductors to terahertz driving.
the phase stiffness of a cuprate superconductor can be controlled via non-linear THz driving, with the in-plane and out-of-plane responses being markedly different.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Josephson plasma waves in cuprates can be excited by THz pulses via a two-plasmon mechanism, even in the absence of the Josephson coupling.
THz light can be used to drive phase excitations, even in the absence of a superfluid response.

THz light can be used to control the superfluid response in unconventional superconducting materials, and that the anisotropic Josephson coupling plays a crucial role in the emergence of non-thermal effects.
